sentences.text: The skulls of these creatures were long and narrow, holding nearly 64 teeth that grew increasingly crowded toward the ends of the jaws.
Unlike some related flying reptiles, the upper jaw curved slightly upward, ending in a small hooked beak no larger than the surrounding teeth.
A long neck was covered in long, bristle-like pycnofibres, a type of hair-like feather found on early birds and pterosaurs.
One specimen preserves a soft tissue crest extending above the eye and the back half of the nasoantorbital fenestra, measuring 44 to 51 mm in length with a height of 9.5 mm.
The rear of the skull featured a small, cone-shaped lappet pointing backward, while another structure resembled an ear tuft.

Webbing connected the fingers and toes, with a membrane spanning the feet and tail, and another between the wrist and shoulder. The claws were encased in keratin sheaths that curved into sharp hooks extending well beyond the bone.
All six known fossils are complete skeletons of juveniles, offering a rare glimpse into the early life of this animal.
The name Aerodactylus means 'wind finger' and was chosen by its describers because it sounds like the Pokémon Aerodactyl.

Fossils of Aerodactylus scolopaciceps are found exclusively in the Solnhofen limestone of Bavaria, Germany, dating to the late Jurassic Period between 150.8 and 148.5 million years ago. In 2014, Vidovic and Martill described Aerodactylus as a new genus based on six juvenile specimens previously attributed to Pterodactylus.
The sharp, keratin-covered claws suggest the animal was adapted for gripping surfaces or prey.
Aerodactylus is classified within the family Aurorazhdarchidae and belongs to the broader parent group Aurorazhdarchidae. It is also classified as a reptile.
These animals lived during the late Jurassic Period between 150.8 and 148.5 million years ago in what is now Bavaria, Germany.

The validity of Aerodactylus is disputed, with some experts suggesting its specimens cannot be distinguished from Pterodactylus. Bennett argued that Aerodactylus is a junior synonym of Pterodactylus because the skull differences are trivial and the specimens represent individual variation rather than a distinct species. In 2024, Smyth and Unwin agreed with Bennett, concluding that Aerodactylus scolopaciceps consists of juvenile Pterodactylus antiquus specimens.
